milestone: Brownie Runtime Boundary And Release DoD Alignment

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Keeps autonomous runtime completion decisions tied to runtime-owned DoD rather than hosted control-plane or adapter product readiness.
Separates runtime permission and tool authority from external scheduler, forge, notification, and commercial operations responsibilities.
Preserves controlled local tool boundaries while keeping forge and hosted product integrations outside Runtime Release DoD.

answers.new_capability: Runtime Product DoD and technical debt evidence now classify responsibility domains so external readiness cannot block Runtime release.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Previous evidence could describe scheduler, hosted operations, forge adapters, or commercial readiness as required_before_release without a machine-checkable runtime boundary.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could keep treating external platform work as unresolved Runtime Product DoD and delay Runtime release for non-runtime features.
answers.non_duplicative: This changes runtime validation, protocol shape, VSIX guards, CI guards, and specs rather than adding another report or roadmap.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Existing product evidence, product completion decision, and protocol validation paths are extended with bounded metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. No report, readiness, digest, history, verdict, summary, or inspection-only surface is added.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime rejects external-domain required Product DoD gaps and external-domain blocking or required_before_release technical debt before product completion evidence is accepted.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous completion can stop on Runtime release readiness while still carrying nonblocking external or commercial readiness debt forward.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the release-boundary ambiguity before any new feature roadmap or commercial control-plane work.

reject_when: phase implements a scheduler, daemon, job queue, hosted worker fleet, tenant service, billing system, monitoring dashboard, forge app, notification adapter, or commercial control-plane product
phase weakens Runtime ownership of task state, Mode Pack materialization, permission checks, tool execution, workspace mutation, replay, recovery, completion, or finalization
phase lets external control-plane, external adapter, or commercial solution debt use blocking or required_before_release classification
phase lets non-runtime Product DoD gaps use required=true
phase collapses Git remote, push, forge API, PR create/update, or PR merge into local process_exec or local Git inspect/commit authority
phase claims total Product Completion instead of bounded Runtime release boundary correction
phase exposes raw prompt, provider response, file content, full diff, stdout, stderr, command, environment value, secret, absolute path, or canonical path

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RBD-1 updates the product-completion guard to require explicit Runtime Release DoD and external readiness separation without weakening evidence or wrapper-only rejection.

exit_criteria: Runtime responsibilities are documented separately from External Control Plane and External Adapter responsibilities.
Run Request, Runtime Event, Control Command, and Run Result or Attestation boundary contracts are documented as Runtime release requirements.
Product Completion Gate requires release_readiness_scope metadata that separates Runtime Release DoD from Commercial Solution Readiness.
Runtime technical debt carry-forward records include responsibility_domain with backward-compatible runtime default.
Runtime rejects external-domain blocking or required_before_release technical debt before Product Completion acceptance.
Runtime rejects external-domain required Product DoD gaps before product evidence matrix derivation.
VSIX protocol validators accept the bounded responsibility_domain fields and reject external-domain release blockers.
Guard tests prove missing release scope and external required-before-release debt are rejected.
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime project_completion_policy_rejects_external_required_runtime_gap proves external Product DoD gaps cannot be required Runtime release gaps.
cargo test -p brownie-runtime technical_debt_carry_forward_rejects_external_release_blockers proves external debt cannot be required_before_release.
cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_run_drive_records_product_complete_decision proves external post_v0 readiness debt remains visible without blocking Runtime product_complete.
node --test scripts/guard-product-completion.test.mjs proves the guard rejects missing release scope and external required-before-release debt.
VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests prove responsibility_domain fields are accepted for runtime payloads and rejected when external required gaps attempt to block.

runtime_release_dod: Durable task, run, journey, checkpoint, ledger, and replay authority.
AgentModes Mode Pack validation, pinning, and permission materialization.
Point-of-use permissions, controlled tools, workspace proposal/apply, approval, completion, and finalization.
Run Request, Runtime Event, Control Command, and Run Result or Attestation contracts.
commercial_solution_readiness: Scheduler, daemon, job queue, worker fleet, leases, hosted isolation, tenants, Secret Provider product, metrics, alerts, SLA, billing, forge apps, notifications, customer admin UI, and broad language adapter catalog.
does_not_close: New hosted scheduler or permanent daemon
GitHub App or GitLab product integration
Monitoring, SLA, billing, or customer admin UI

technical_debt.evidence: Tracked outside Runtime Release DoD; not required_before_release for Brownie Runtime.
Forge PR and notification products remain adapter readiness, not Runtime release blockers.
Schedulers, workers, leases, hosted isolation, and concrete Secret Provider integrations remain external control-plane readiness.

accepted_capability: Runtime Product DoD gap responsibility validation.
VSIX and guard protocol enforcement for the same boundary.
behavior_evidence: Runtime tests cover external required Product DoD gap rejection, external required-before-release debt rejection, and nonblocking external post_v0 carry-forward.
Product completion guard tests cover release_readiness_scope and external debt classification rejection.
VSIX protocol tests cover bounded responsibility_domain acceptance and rejection.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains authority for Product DoD selection, debt carry-forward, completion refusal, replay, and idempotency.
External control-plane, adapter, and commercial readiness entries cannot grant runtime permissions or block Runtime release.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection surfaces and do not own runtime release policy.
No raw prompt, provider response, raw file content, full diff, stdout, stderr, command, environment value, secret, absolute path, or canonical path is exposed.
non_goals: No scheduler, daemon, permanent polling loop, job queue, worker fleet, or hosted control-plane product.
No Docker, Kubernetes, VM, Vault, tenant, admin UI, metrics, alerts, SLA, billing, or Secret Provider product.
No GitHub App, GitLab adapter, PR creation workflow, notification adapter, or broad language verifier catalog.
No remote Git push, PR merge capability, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or recursive Brownie invocation.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected treating Commercial Solution Readiness as Runtime required_before_release debt.
Rejected implementing hosted control-plane features to satisfy Runtime release DoD.
Rejected docs-only boundary correction without runtime and guard validation.
Rejected collapsing local Git and forge adapter capabilities into process_exec.
technical_debt: External control-plane productization remains post_v0 commercial readiness.
External forge and notification adapters remain post_v0 adapter readiness.
Hosted operations and language adapter breadth remain post_v0 commercial readiness.
next_capability_rationale: After review, Brownie Runtime release readiness can be assessed against runtime contracts only; commercial solution readiness can be planned separately.

runtime_release_dod: Durable task/run/journey state, checkpoint, ledger, idempotency, stale rejection, replay, conflict, and cancellation safety.
Agent loop execution, Mode Pack validation/pinning/materialization, permissions, controlled tools, workspace proposal/apply, approvals, and completion/finalization.
Product DoD selection and closure, runtime-domain debt carry-forward, and bounded refusal/blocker machinery.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduler, daemon, job queue, worker fleet, leases, retry policy, hosted isolation, Secret Provider product, metrics, alerts, SLA, HA, tenants, and billing.
external_adapter_responsibilities: GitHub App, GitLab adapter, PR create/update/merge workflows, Slack, Teams, email, SIEM, OTel, customer systems, and language-specific verifier adapter breadth.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, operations, enterprise administration, hosted supportability, and customer-facing commercial readiness beyond Runtime release.
